Subject: Sales discovery: model fit & next steps

Hi Sarah / Michael,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about Acme's in-product assistant use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap:
- Goal: multi-turn product Q&A + summarization for user sessions tied to catalog items (sensitive PII redaction required).
- Target latency: <200ms p95 for UI-affecting calls; typical request size ~40–80 tokens.
- Expected concurrency: bursts up to ~50 concurrent users; baseline steady-state ~10 req/sec.
- Quality priority: high factuality for catalog details (price, specs).

Suggested models (initial):
- redwood-4b-quant (low-latency, cost-efficient) — recommended for UI-critical paths.
- redwood-13b-qat (best quality / good perf with quantization) — recommended for highest accuracy flows.
- fallback: redwood-30b-enc (if additional quality required; higher latency/cost).

I'll loop in Marissa (benchmarks) with Redwood-verified performance profiles and prompt-set examples for your eval. Next steps:
1) Marissa to share benchmark links + recommended prompt set by EOD.
2) Align on a short eval (1–2k requests) and success metrics (p95 latency, answer accuracy on 300 sample prompts).
3) Quick 30-min follow-up to finalize procurement/MAP.

Attachments: I'll include the prompt set sample once Marissa adds it to the thread.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Sarah / Michael —

Attaching the initial artifacts for your eval and answers to your Qs. Links and attachments below:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3CREDWOOD-BENCHMARKS (contains CSVs, raw numbers, and the prompt set)
- Public report (redwood_verified_profiles_acme.pdf) attached — summary of 4b / 13b perf on both Dedicated A100-80 and our hosted tiers.
- prompt set: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached) — 300 curated prompts across QA, clarifying Qs, and summarization.

Key Redwood-verified performance highlights (numbers are measured on Redwood Dedicated A100-80GB pools, median of multiple runs; results vary by seq length + batching):
- redwood-4b-quant (Q4_0): avg request size 64 tokens
  - TPS (requests/sec): 95
  - p50 latency: 14 ms
  - p95 latency: 48 ms
  - Notes: excellent for UI paths; highest cost-efficiency.

- redwood-13b-qat (Q4_1, quantized-activation): avg request size 64 tokens
  - TPS (requests/sec): 28
  - p50 latency: 38 ms
  - p95 latency: 132 ms
  - Notes: better factuality and instruction-following; p95 under 200ms in most configs if you pin model on Dedicated.

- redwood-30b-enc (non-quantized) — reference only
  - TPS (requests/sec): 8
  - p50 latency: 110 ms
  - p95 latency: 280 ms

Recommendations based on your targets:
- If Acme needs UI latency p95 <200ms and wants the best balance of accuracy/cost, start with redwood-13b-qat pinned to Dedicated with Q4_1. We'll configure automatic fallback to redwood-4b-quant for ultra-low-latency UI micro-interactions (e.g., live typeahead).
- Use prefix/KV caching for user-session context to reduce per-request tokens — this typically increases observed TPS by 20–40% for repeat patterns.
- For PII: use Redwood Private or Dedicated with KMS integration and S3 encryption enabled; retention policy can be set to zero retention for request/response logs if required. I'll loop in Security if you want the SOC2 artifacts.

Attachments included: redwood_verified_profiles_acme.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl.

Also linking an internal benchmark visualization for quick view: https://openbench.co/reports/acme-202608

Next steps I propose:
- Quick 30-min sync to walk through the prompt set and confirm success metrics. Alex, can you propose 2 times?
- We'll provision a short Dedicated eval (48–72 hours) based on your estimate of concurrency and token budget.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Product PM, Benchmarks | Redwood Inference
